gaps.sentence: After three attempts, she ___ pass her driving test at last.
gaps.explanation: A specific past success takes 'was able to' or 'managed to': was able to pass.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: Need we ___ the whole report, or just the summary?
gaps.hint: modal need takes the bare infinitive
gaps.explanation: When 'need' is a modal in questions and negatives, it takes the bare infinitive: read.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.
